name: overflow-count
purpose: A small `+N` chip that stands for the items a slot cannot show, and opens a popover with the whole list. It replaces the design sample's `DomainOverflowPopover`, the overflow badge of `TagListCell` and `WorkloadCell`, and the Console Kit's `OverflowCountButton`. The popover follows the overflow rule of `webkit-ux-heuristics`: a summary line (`12 domains`, `10 of 34 domains` while paged), a search box once the list holds more than 7 items, a scrolling list, a **Load N more** footer while items remain, a no-match line quoting the query, and a polite status region that announces the summary. Closing it clears the query and the paging.
useWhen: A table cell or a detail row shows the first value of a list and the rest hide behind a count: the domains of a workload, the tags of a row, the workloads a rule applies to.
A card or a header names one item of many and the reader may want the full list without leaving the screen.
avoidWhen: The list is the content of the page → render it as a `Table` or an `Item` list.
The reader picks from the list → use `Select`, `Combobox` or `MultiSelect`.
A single count without a list behind it → use `Badge`.
related: table` — `Table.CellTags` and `Table.CellLink` put this chip after the values they fit.
tag` — the chip is a small secondary `Tag`.
popover` — the list opens in a `Popover`.
bestPractices: Show the first item (or as many as fit) beside the chip; the chip counts only the hidden ones, and `items` passes only those.
Name the items with `noun` (`{ one: 'domain', other: 'domains' }`) so the summary reads `12 domains`, not `12 items`.
Give an item an `href` only when it opens something; an item without one renders as plain text.
Use the `item` slot for a router link or a richer entry; keep every entry to one truncating line.

props.name: items
props.doc: The hidden items. The chip reads `+<length>`; an item with `href` opens in a new tab.

props.name: noun
props.doc: What the items are, for the summary and the trigger's name. Empty uses the catalog (`item` / `items`).

slots.name: item
slots.notes: One list entry; replaces the built-in text or link.
